transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, honestly, what made me come in is... I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. Like, I'll sit with my husband or try to watch my shows after work, and I know I should feel comfort or even a little happy, but... there’s just nothing there right now.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yeah, it did. Um, it's been going on for about three weeks now, ever since... well, a heavy pallet collapsed at work and injured my coworker. It started right after that.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
Not really sad, no. I mean... I wouldn't say I'm feeling down or crying all day. It's really just that blank feeling I mentioned. I just don't feel much of anything at all.
Since the accident, have unwanted memories of it been popping into your mind?

Yeah, they have. Out of nowhere, I'll just see that pallet coming down again, or... or I'll hear the crash in my head. It happens a lot at work, especially if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something in the warehouse. Whenever it happens, my stomach just turns.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid reminders of what happened?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still have to go to work every day and do my job. So I'm still right there in the warehouse, around the pallets and the forklifts. I haven't really been trying to stay away from any of it, even though it bothers me when I'm there.
Since the accident, have you been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled?

No, not really. I mean... I haven't noticed myself jumping at things or being more startled than usual. Like I said, the noises at work bother me and bring the memories back, but I don't physically jump or feel on edge like that. So, no, I don't think so.
Since the accident, have you been trying not to think about it or push the feelings about it away?

No, I don't think I do that. Um, I mean, I don't really try to block it out or anything. When it pops into my head, it just happens. I'm not actively trying to push the thoughts or the feelings away. I just kind of deal with it when it comes up.
Since the accident, have you felt detached from yourself, like you were outside yourself or unreal?
No, I haven't felt anything like that. Um, I feel like myself. I haven't had any moments where I felt like I was outside my body or like things weren't real. I just feel normal in that way, I guess.
Since the accident, has this been making it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yeah, it has. I mean, I'm actually not able to do my regular receiving work right now. Um... I was doing a pallet move recently and I just froze up, and then I ended up snapping at someone. My supervisor had to take me off the floor after that because I just wasn't functioning safely out there. So, yeah, it's definitely making things hard at work.
Did these feelings start right away after the accident?
Yeah, pretty much. It's been going on for about three weeks now. It all started right after that day when the pallet collapsed and my coworker got hurt. So, yeah, ever since then.
Since the accident, have your reactions felt stronger than you would have expected for what happened?

Yeah, I guess so. I've just been... snapping at people over really small stuff. Like, the other day, one of the seasonal guys set some boxes down just a little crooked, and I just went off. I hear myself getting sharp and loud before I can even pull it back. It's just... I don't normally react like that, but lately, it's like I have no patience at all.
Has it been more than one month since the accident?
No, not quite a month yet. Like I mentioned a little bit ago, it's been about three weeks. Just... ever since that day the pallet collapsed and injured my coworker.
Have these reactions been causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah, it really has. I mean, it's messing up my job. I'm not even able to do my regular receiving work right now. After I snapped at that seasonal guy, and then... well, I completely froze up during another pallet move. My supervisor had to step in and actually take me off the floor. He told me I just wasn't functioning safely. So, yeah, it's definitely causing a lot of problems for me.
Since the accident, have there been times when you felt emotionally numb, like you couldn’t feel love, happiness, or closeness?

Yeah, that's... actually, that's kind of what made me finally come in here. It's like the warm part of me just shut off completely. I'll sit with my husband in the evenings, or try to watch my regular shows after work, and I know I should feel some comfort, or at least a little bit happy to just be home. But... there's just nothing there. I just feel empty.
Have these symptoms already started to get better?

No, not really. I keep hoping I'll wake up and just feel normal again, but... no, they haven't gotten any better. It's pretty much been exactly the same since the accident. I haven't noticed any improvement yet.
Since the accident, have there been times when you felt dazed or less aware of what was going on around you?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt dazed or anything like that. I mean, I'm pretty aware of what's going on around me, maybe even more than usual. But no, I haven't felt spaced out or less aware.
Did your symptoms start within a few minutes of seeing the pallet collapse?

No, I wouldn't say it was within a few minutes. Right after the pallet collapsed, I was mostly just... running on adrenaline, I think. Just trying to figure out what happened and making sure everything was handled. It didn't really start hitting me until later on.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding parts of the warehouse where the pallet collapsed?
No, I haven't really done that. I mean, I still have to do my job, so I go where I need to go. I haven't been avoiding that specific area or anything. I just... do my work.
Since the accident, have you been pulling away from other people more than usual?
No, I don't think so. I still talk to the other people on my shift just like normal, and I'm around my family when I get home. I haven't really felt the need to isolate myself or anything like that.
Right when you saw the pallet collapse, did you feel intense fear, helplessness, or horror?

No, not really. I mean, it was definitely startling, and I was worried about whether anyone got hurt, but I wouldn't say I felt... horrified or helpless. It was just a really big mess that happened all of a sudden, and my first thought was just that we needed to clean it up and report it.
